Wellbeing before and during the COVID-19 pandemic (simulated panel)

wellbeing_panel.Rd

Sleep, physical activity, stress and loneliness of 700 adults in 2019, 2020 and 2021, designed for latent transition analysis with continuous indicators and partial measurement invariance across waves (lta() with indicators = "continuous").

Usage

wellbeing_panel

Format

A data frame with 700 rows and 15 columns:

id

Respondent id.

sleep_1, sleep_2, sleep_3

Hours of sleep per night in 2019, 2020, 2021.

activity_1, activity_2, activity_3

Hours of moderate-to-vigorous activity per week.

stress_1, stress_2, stress_3

Perceived Stress Scale (PSS-4), 0–16.

lonely_1, lonely_2, lonely_3

UCLA 3-item loneliness scale, 3–9.

female

1 = woman.

age

Age in years at wave 1.

The columns are ordered by wave: sleep_1, activity_1, stress_1, lonely_1, sleep_2, .... Monotone attrition: 6 percent have only wave 1, a further 10 percent waves 1–2.

Source

Simulated by datasets/generate.jl of LatentMixtures.jl (seed Xoshiro(20261103)); codebook in its datasets/README.md. Three profiles, Thriving (means sleep 7.5, activity 5.5, stress 4.0, lonely 3.8), Typical (7.0, 3.2, 6.5, 4.8) and Struggling (6.0, 1.5, 10.0, 6.8), standard deviations 0.8, 1.6, 2.0, 1.0. In 2020 stress (+1.5) and loneliness (+1.0) are higher in every profile: a wave-specific shift of the measurement intercepts, so freeing the means of items 3 and 4 at wave 2 is the true model. Initial shares 0.35, 0.40, 0.25; transition matrices (rows: from) 2019 to 2020 [.80 .15 .05; .10 .75 .15; .05 .20 .75], 2020 to 2021 [.85 .12 .03; .15 .75 .10; .08 .25 .67]. Licence: CC0 1.0 (public domain).

Examples

data(wellbeing_panel)
# mean stress and loneliness rose in the pandemic year 2020
colMeans(wellbeing_panel[, c("stress_1", "stress_2", "stress_3")], na.rm = TRUE)
#> stress_1 stress_2 stress_3 
#> 6.412714 8.003664 6.461929 
# \donttest{
# latent transitions between three wellbeing profiles, with the 2020 means of stress
# and loneliness free (partial measurement invariance)
wb <- list(sleep_1:lonely_1, sleep_2:lonely_2, sleep_3:lonely_3)
#> Error: object 'sleep_1' not found
t3 <- lta(wellbeing_panel, waves = wb, K = 3, indicators = "continuous",
          invariance = list(stress_1 = 2, lonely_1 = 2))
#> Error: object 'wb' not found
profilemeans(t3, wave = 1)   # Thriving, Typical and Struggling profiles (sorted by size)
#> Error: object 't3' not found
transitions(t3)[[1]]
#> Error: object 't3' not found
# }
